title: SCALE: A Structure-Centric Accelerator for Message Passing Graph Neural Networks
problem: Message passing GNNs suffer from heterogeneous computation kernels with inconsistent edge and vertex operations, creating challenges in data reuse, workload balance across different operation types, and system scalability.
motivation: GNNs are critical for complex deep learning models, but their computational heterogeneity and diverse variants impose substantial implementation and scalability challenges that hardware accelerators can address.
method: Different GNN models perform different operations, but they share common patterns in how data moves through computations. SCALE takes a structure-centric approach, designing hardware around these shared dataflow patterns rather than optimizing each model separately. It combines three techniques: a systolic array-like processor (a grid of coordinated units) supporting varied dataflows including all-reduce operations (combining results from multiple units), scheduling that considers vertex degree (how many connections each node has) to balance workload, and a unified data pipeline for both graph and neural operations without extra overhead.
key_novelty: Different GNN models share underlying dataflow patterns (how data flows through operations), so hardware optimized for those universal patterns can work across all models instead of separate model-specific designs.
contributions: Systolic array-like architecture supporting multiple dataflow patterns for improved parallelism and data reuse in GNNs
Degree and vertex-aware scheduling algorithm to remedy workload imbalance in edge and vertex operations
Unified dataflow for fused graph and neural operations without additional communication or storage costs
Achieves 1.82× average speedup and 38.9% energy reduction over state-of-the-art GNN accelerators
primary_theme: Hardware accelerator for graph neural networks
